title: How do we write the area of the dashed region?
description: The dashed region is a rectangle with a strip of width r cut along one side and one end. Its area is written in two ways, the two are matched by multiplying out, and the area is found for p as six, r as three point five and s as nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: the region left is a smaller rectangle, and the whole take away two strips needs the corner added back. Watch for students who take the corner away twice.

source: Math Talk (area of the dashed region)
video_script.why: The child has matched the areas of one region found in different ways, and now does the same with letters for the dashed region.
video_script.substitution: Write the dashed area as a smaller rectangle, then as the whole take away two strips with the corner added back, multiply out to match them, and put in the numbers.
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with sides p and s, a strip of width r taken away along one side and one end, and the dashed region left
video_script.payoff_line: Its area is p minus r, times s minus r, which is thirteen point seven five square units

final_answer.value: (p − r)(s − r) = ps − pr − sr + r²; the area is 13.75 square units
final_answer.spoken: p minus r, times s minus r, which is thirteen point seven five square units

never_show: ps − pr − sr as the area, marked as right
maths_rules: the rectangle has sides p and s; a strip of width r is taken along one side and one end
way 1: the dashed region is a rectangle with sides (p − r) and (s − r), area (p − r)(s − r)
way 2: ps − pr − sr + r², because the corner r by r lies in both strips and is taken away twice
(p − r)(s − r) = ps − pr − rs + r², since (− r) × (− r) = + r²; both ways agree
video_script.design: One idea: two ways to the same area. The figure stays all video in the anchor band; the working board holds each way and the numbers.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write its area in more than one way. Then find it when p is six, r is three point five and s is nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='rect'/>First, see the dashed region as one smaller rectangle.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>The strip takes r from each side, so its sides are p minus r and s minus r.
<bookmark mark='area'/>Its area is length times breadth, p minus r times s minus r.

beats.on_screen: Way 2: whole rectangle ps; strip along the side pr; strip along the end sr; corner r² taken away twice; area = ps − pr − sr + r²

marks.whole: the whole rectangle glows and ps is written
marks.strips: the two strips glow and pr and sr are written
marks.corner: the corner square r by r glows where the strips overlap
marks.area: area = ps − pr − sr + r² is written

beats.colours: the two strips in two colours, the corner in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Second, start with the whole rectangle. Its area is p s.
<bookmark mark='strips'/>Take away the strip along the side, p r, and the strip along the end, s r.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>The corner square r by r lies in both strips, so it was taken away twice. Add r squared back.
<bookmark mark='area'/>The area is p s, take away p r, take away s r, plus r squared.

beats.on_screen: (p − r)(s − r) = ps − pr − rs + r², the same as way 2

marks.mul: (p − r)(s − r) = ps − pr − rs + r² is written
marks.sign: (− r) × (− r) = + r² is written beside it
marks.same: the result and way 2 glow together

beats.colours: the two results in matching colours
narration: <bookmark mark='mul'/>Third, multiply out p minus r, times s minus r. We get p s, take away p r, take away r s, plus r squared.
<bookmark mark='sign'/>Minus r times minus r is plus r squared.
<bookmark mark='same'/>This is the same as the second way, so both ways agree.

marks.put: p = 6, r = 3.5 and s = 9 are put into (p − r)(s − r)

narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Fourth, put in p as six, r as three point five and s as nine.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>Six minus three point five is two point five. Nine minus three point five is five point five.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Two point five times five point five is thirteen point seven five.

marks.back: the words check with the second way are written
marks.calc: ps = 54, pr = 21, sr = 31.5 and r² = 12.25 are written, then 54 − 21 − 31.5 + 12.25

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Fifth, put the numbers into the second way to check.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Fifty four take away twenty one is thirty three. Thirty three take away thirty one point five is one point five.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Add twelve point two five to get thirteen point seven five. Both ways agree.
